digest.component_or_area: rebar transition close (completion verification and signing)
propositions: A concurrent git commit landing between verify() and sign() in the close transition causes the ticket to close without a completion signature, because HEAD resolves to different SHAs in each phase and the pre-sign drift guard refuses to sign but does not prevent the close.

The default (no --ref) code path reads HEAD independently in verify and sign steps, creating a TOCTOU window; a benign unrelated commit by another agent in the shared worktree can split verify→sign, leaving the ticket closed unsigned.

The suggested recovery message ('re-close to certify') is a no-op for an already-closed ticket, and the only alternatives are --force-close (undesirable) or manual manifest fabrication (unacceptable).
The close transition should either pin one immutable revision for the entire verify+sign+close unit, or abort and leave the ticket in_progress (retryable) on drift, instead of closing unsigned.
There is no first-class, non-force recovery path to obtain a completion attestation for a ticket that is already closed but unsigned.
